10.1002_adma.75182: Direct recycling of spent lithium‐ion battery (LIB) cathodes holds great promise for sustainable materials recovery. However, residual fluorinated impurities, including inorganic fluoride species and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), remain a persistent challenge due to their chemical persistence and heterogeneous distribution. Here, we report an electrochemically driven self‐cleaning strategy that enables fluoride‐free adaptive direct recycling of spent cathodes. Using LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 (NMC532) as a model system, anodic polarization activates oxygen‐evolution‐driven surface reconstruction, generating hydroxylated transition metal (TM) interfaces that trigger the cooperative elimination of fluorinated contaminants. Specifically, the reconstruction promotes proton‐assisted dissolution of LiF and related inorganic fluoride species, while simultaneously inducing a hydrophobic‐to‐hydrophilic interfacial transition that weakens PVDF adhesion and facilitates its removal. These coupled redox‐hydrolysis‐interfacial processes synergistically eradicate fluorinated residues while preserving the bulk composition and structural integrity of the cathode. The regenerated NMC532 delivers a high discharge capacity of 145.1 mAh·g −1 , comparable to commercial material. When implemented in pouch cells, this strategy achieves an inter‑batch capacity variation of less than 1.3%, dramatically outperforming the ∼24.1% variation typical of conventional recycling and meeting commercial consistency standards (± 3%–5%). This reconstruction‐enabled self‐cleaning strategy is broadly applicable across diverse cathode chemistries, providing a scalable and chemically selective pathway toward impurity‑free, high‑performance battery material regeneration.
10.1016_j.esci.2026.100633: The scalable fabrication of transition metal sulfide (TMS) electrodes with both high electrocatalytic activity and structural robustness remains a significant challenge for the electrocatalytic oxygen evolution reaction. Here, we report a non-equilibrium spray pyrolysis strategy that exploits the rapid decomposition of thiourea to synthesize meter-scale (1.2 × 0.5 m 2 ) Turing-pattern-like TMS electrodes. Concurrent sulfurization of the substrate induces in situ -generated reactive metal–sulfur interfaces, which yield strong catalyst-substrate adhesion. As a representative example, the synthesized Ni 0.75 Fe 0.25 S 2−δ delivers a current density of 1 A cm −2 at a cell voltage of 1.71 V when employed as the anode in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, and sustains operation for 5000 h with limited degradation. The Turing-pattern-like structure increases active site exposure and promotes efficient mass transport. Complementary density functional theory calculations and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that sulfur vacancies facilitate the formation of electrochemically active oxyhydroxide species. This work establishes a versatile strategy for designing advanced electrocatalysts through the synergy of interfacial reinforcement and microstructural engineering, offering a promising pathway toward industrial-scale water electrolysis.
10.1038_s41467-026-78267-5: The differences in crystallization and migration barriers of iodide and bromide within wide-bandgap perovskite result in inhomogeneous crystallization and halogen-phase segregation, limiting photovoltaic device performance. Here we report a sequential regulation engineering to synchronously homogenize crystallization and stabilize crystallographic phase by adding 2-iminothiolane (ITA). ITA priorly undergoes an in situ thiolation reaction with methylamine to yield a reductive 4-mercapto-N-methylformamidine (MMF). It effectively modulates perovskite crystallization toward homogenization, scavenges the detrimental molecular iodine or iodine radicals by redox reaction, and anchors the migratory iodide ions by hydrogen-bond interaction. Leveraging these contributions, the obtained perovskite films exhibit the suppressed halogen phase and enhanced ion migration barrier along the vacancy and interstitial defects-depending migration paths, achieving an efficiency of 20.45%. Moreover, the corresponding champion tandem solar cell (TSC) achieves an efficiency of 28.20% (certified 27.82%), retaining 90% initial efficiency by continuous tracking maximum power point after 700 h under ISOS-L-1 protocol. Inhomogeneous crystallization and phase segregation in wide-bandgap perovskite limit the performance of photovoltaic device. Zhu et al. develop an in situ sequential regulation strategy for crystallization, achieving a power conversion efficiency of 28.20% for perovskite-organic tandem solar cells.
